message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip or reorder sections if you already have some components or experience.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you need (gaming, office, content creation) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. |
| 2 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, aesthetics, and future upgrade space. | Pick ATX mid‑tower for most builds; ensure it has enough drive bays and cable management options. |
| 3 | **Select a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components; must be reliable and efficient. | Look for 80+ Bronze or better, 80+ Gold for higher efficiency. Size: 500W–750W for mid‑range builds; 650W+ for gaming rigs. |
| 4 | **Pick a Motherboard** | Hosts CPU, RAM, storage, expansion slots, and connectivity. | Match socket type with CPU (e.g., LGA 1200 for Intel 10th‑gen, AM4 for AMD Ryzen 3000‑4000). Check BIOS version support for your CPU. |
| 5 | **Choose a CPU** | Core performance, clock speed, integrated graphics (if needed). | For gaming: Ryzen 5 5600X or Intel i5‑12400F. For content creation: Ryzen 7 5800X or Intel i7‑12700K. |
| 6 | **Get RAM** | Speed and capacity affect multitasking and gaming. | 16GB DDR4 (3200–3600 MHz) is a sweet spot. Dual‑channel kits (two sticks) give better performance. |
| 7 | **Select Storage** | SSDs are faster; HDDs offer more cheap space. | NVMe M.2 SSD (PCIe 3.0/4.0) for OS + games; SATA SSD for additional storage. |
| 8 | **Graphics Card (GPU)** | Needed for gaming, video editing, AI workloads. | Choose based on GPU memory (VRAM) and performance tier. For 1080p gaming: RTX 3060 or RX 6600 XT. For 1440p/4K: RTX 3070/3080 or RX 6800/6900 XT. |
| 9 | **Cooling Solution** | Keeps CPU temperatures low, improves longevity. | Stock coolers are fine for low‑power CPUs; aftermarket air coolers or AIO liquid coolers for overclocking. |
|10 | **Operating System** | Windows 11/10, Linux, etc. | Windows 11 Home/Pro for gaming; Ubuntu or Fedora for developers. |
|11 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Screwdrivers, anti‑static wrist strap, clean surface. | Keep screws organized; use a magnetic tray or labeled containers. |
|12 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs, route cables early. | Clean dust filters; label cable routing paths. |
|13 | **Install the PSU** | Mount it, connect main power cables. | Ensure the PSU fan faces outward for airflow. |
|14 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align with standoffs, screw in. | Double‑check orientation of I/O shield. |
|15 | **Insert the CPU** | Open the socket latch, align the triangle marker, gently place. | Avoid touching pins; use a soft cloth. |
|16 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | Even heat transfer from CPU to cooler. | Use a pea‑size amount; spread evenly. |
|17 | **Install RAM** | Snap into DIMM slots. | Insert both sticks simultaneously for dual‑channel. |
|18 | **Mount Storage** | Secure SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | Use screws or tool‑free brackets. |
|19 | **Install GPU** | Slide into PCIe x16 slot, secure with screws. | Connect 8‑pin/6‑pin power connectors. |
|20 | **Connect Front Panel & USB** | Attach power button, reset, USB ports, audio jacks. | Refer to motherboard manual for pin layout. |
|21 | **Cable Management** | Route cables neatly, use zip ties. | Keep airflow unobstructed; avoid blocking fans. |
|22 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Verify all power, data, and front panel connections. | Inspect for loose screws or bent pins. |
|23 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | Boot, enter BIOS, set boot order, enable XMP for RAM. | Update BIOS if needed before installing OS. |
|24 | **Install Operating System** | Create bootable USB, install OS, install drivers. | Install chipset, GPU, and other drivers first. |
|25 | **Install Software & Updates** | Install essential apps, updates, antivirus. | Keep system updated for security and performance. |
|26 | **Test & Benchmark** | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark) to confirm stability. | Monitor temperatures; ensure they stay within safe limits. |
|27 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep dust‑free, update drivers, monitor temperatures. | Schedule periodic cleaning and firmware updates. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Case
- [ ] PSU
- [ ] Motherboard
- [ ] CPU
- [ ] RAM
- [ ] Storage (NVMe + SATA)
- [ ] GPU
- [ ] Cooling (air or liquid)
- [ ] OS
- [ ] Tools (Phillips screwdriver, anti‑static strap)
- [ ] Cable ties / Velcro straps
- [ ] Dust filters

#### Common Pitfalls & Fixes

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **CPU not seated** | Re‑open the socket, align correctly, close latch. |
| **GPU not recognized** | Check power connectors, reseat in PCIe slot. |
| **No POST** | Verify power supply, check all cables, test PSU with a PSU tester. |
| **High temperatures** | Reapply thermal paste, improve cable routing, add case fans. |
| **Fan noise** | Tighten screws, replace noisy fans, use anti‑vibration mounts. |

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build lists, price tracking, compatibility checks.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc, r/pcmasterrace for community help.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always keep the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals handy.

Happy building! If you hit a snag or need component recommendations, just let me know.
